legend.mapchallenge.populationNote: Only cells with density ≥100 are drawn (2,773 cells, about 5.2 km² each). Population is the GHSL 2020 model estimate, not household registration.
legend.mapchallenge.facilityNote: Only cells with density ≥100 are drawn (about 5.2 km² each); each facility type has its own color ramp and fixed class breaks.
legend.mapchallenge.overlapNote: Hotspot = top 10% of populated cells in Taiwan (about 5.2 km² each). Overlap = share of population hotspots that are also facility hotspots.
legend.mapchallenge.tcchNote: Hotspot = top 10% within each county (about 0.74 km² fine cells); the two counties are not compared with each other.
legend.mapchallenge.source: GHSL GHS-POP R2023A 2020 (CC BY 4.0), MOEA factory registry 2026-06, MOI temple registry, MOE school directory, MOHW medical facilities, cram school directory, OpenStreetMap (ODbL, convenience stores); taipei-gis-analytics Day 4 cluster analysis
legend.mapchallenge.day05.method: Estimated from terrain + buildings + tree canopy; a view counts as continuous at ≥500 m with gaps ≤200 m; Green Island, Xiaoliuqiu, Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu not covered
legend.mapchallenge.day05.source: Terrain: MOI 20 m digital terrain model (2024); building height: GBA/OSM fusion; canopy height: Meta/WRI (CC BY 4.0); routes: OpenStreetMap (ODbL)
legend.mapchallenge.day05.seaViewNote: Rail is drawn thicker than roads; only routes within 3 km of the sea are shown. Trees within 40 m of the road are counted from 10 m canopy data (Meta/WRI); seawalls and coastal windbreak forests use assumed heights; the sea is taken at high tide (tidal flats count as sea); "through trees" means the view is partly blocked.
legend.mapchallenge.day06.source: Present-day data: OpenStreetMap coastline (ODbL, retrieved 2026-11-06); MOI place names (2026-10-12) and village boundaries (2026-06-26); MOI national religion registry temples (retrieved 2026-08-01); Pulse lighthouse layer and CWA station list (update date not checked)
legend.mapchallenge.day06.places: Today's place names with 鯤鯓 / 塭 / 汕 (sandbar, fish pond, shoal); colour = latest era in which the spot was still west of the coastline
legend.mapchallenge.day06.coastNote: The three eras use three distinct hues; the oldest (17th–18th c.) line is drawn thicker. All three trace water/land boundaries including lagoons such as the Taijiang Inner Sea; the 19th-century line reaches as far inland as the 17th–18th century one around 23.05–23.15°N (original notes not checked).
legend.mapchallenge.day06.coastToday: Within the range shared by all three eras, median distance from the furthest inland water to today's outer coast: about 17.9 km (17th–18th c.), 7.6 km (19th c.), 2.0 km (early 20th c.).
legend.mapchallenge.day06.surviveYes: Name survives in today's village names ({n})
legend.mapchallenge.day06.taipeiNote: 74 towns (machi) and ōaza; a name counts as surviving when its stem appears in an overlapping present-day village name (e.g. Nishimon → Ximen Village). Names shown from z12; datum error about 50 m.
legend.mapchallenge.day06.templeTitle: Temples that stayed: 1921 shrines and temples
legend.mapchallenge.day06.templeYes: A registered temple within 100 m today
legend.mapchallenge.day06.templeSame: Same name today: a temple of the same name nearby ({n})
legend.mapchallenge.day06.templeNote: 1,007 of 1,439 (70%) still have a registered temple within 100 m; shifting every point 300 or 600 m gives only about 9%. Unregistered small shrines are missing from today's list, so this is a lower bound. The {n} named sites with a same-name temple today are ringed and labelled from z13.
legend.mapchallenge.day06.lighthouseTitl: Lighthouses and weather stations, then and now
legend.mapchallenge.day06.lighthouseNote: All five weather stations set up in 1896–97 are still staffed CWA stations; Taipei is only 10 m away. Today's list has only 36 main lighthouses, so 'no match' does not mean gone; the Pengjia Islet point lies at sea and is treated as a digitising error.
legend.mapchallenge.day06.sourceShort: Academia Sinica, Taiwan History and Culture in Atlas, 1st ed. (2003), CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 Taiwan; derived data under the same terms (non-commercial)
legend.mapchallenge.day08.caveat: Research estimate, not an official appraisal; 2024 population held fixed
legend.mapchallenge.day08.source: Sources: MOI statistical-area population (2024), OpenStreetMap parks and roads (ODbL), Taipei City flood-gate open data (data.gov.tw 143891), New Taipei zoning, MOI real-price registry, national land-use survey
legend.mapchallenge.day08.accessTitle: Walking Minutes to a Large Park (Zhonghe + Yonghe)
legend.mapchallenge.day08.accessNote: Walking minutes along the road network to the nearest park of ≥1 ha, riverside parks included but reachable only through the entrances that cross the levee; >30 min or unreachable is recorded as 30. General: all residents at 4.8 km/h; children & elderly: ages 65+ and 0–14 at 3.6 km/h.
legend.mapchallenge.day08.sitesTitle: New Park Sites and Their Cost
legend.mapchallenge.day08.sitesNote: A Efficiency, B Equity and B2 Children & Elderly First each pick 5 sites; C picks 5 sites only from park land not yet built (greedy; people still live on some of it). Total cost covers land, buildings, household payments and park works, as low / base / high.
legend.mapchallenge.day08.sitesNoteHist: D / Dfull are geometric counterfactuals: the cost of buying back the parks (and green belts) of the 1955 plan today, had they been kept. Not a reenactment of history. School sites are not shown.
legend.mapchallenge.day08.planLicense: 1955 Zhonghe Town Plan Map, CC BY-NC 3.0 TW, Taiwan Cultural Memory Bank (Yonghe Community College)
legend.mapchallenge.day08.planOffset: Position may be off by about 30–55 m
legend.mapchallenge.day08.sitesNone: No new sites in the current state; switch to A / B / B2 / C / D / Dfull.
legend.mapchallenge.day08.entranceRule: Riverside parks can only be entered through openings in the levee: footbridges, underpasses, stairs over the levee and flood gates. Entrances are inferred from the OpenStreetMap pedestrian network. New Taipei has no open flood-gate list (Taipei uses the Taipei City flood-gate open data), and gates OSM does not tag are missed, so this is a conservative lower bound. Gates closed during typhoons are not modelled.
legend.mapchallenge.day08.parksSource: Sources: OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Taipei City flood-gate open data (data.gov.tw 143891)
legend.mapchallenge.day09.densityUnit: 368 townships split into five groups by population density (people/km²), about 74 each
legend.mapchallenge.day09.ratioSub: Sites per 10,000 people vs. national average ({n} per 10,000); brighter = more per person
legend.mapchallenge.day09.bin0: ¼ of national average or less
legend.mapchallenge.day09.cvsNote: Counts only 7-Eleven, FamilyMart, Hi-Life and OK stores with a bank ATM (estimated from the FISC ATM list); outlying islands may be undercounted, so 0 does not mean no store
legend.mapchallenge.day09.hcNote: Only health centers with NHI outpatient clinics; Taipei's health service centers are not on the list, so 0 in cities reflects the list, not an absence
legend.mapchallenge.day09.groupNote: Urban-rural groups are custom density quintiles, not an official classification; single-period data, and having a site in the township does not mean it is easy to reach
legend.mapchallenge.day09.source: Sources: Ministry of the Interior household registration (2026-08-31), Ministry of Education, National Police Agency, Chunghwa Post, NHIA, FISC
legend.mapchallenge.day17.skySub: Estimated sky glow (relative, Taipei Main Station = 1), 5 classes
legend.mapchallenge.day17.skyBreaks: Breaks: {a} / {b} / {c} / {d}; class 1 = darkest 20% of Taiwan's land
legend.mapchallenge.day17.skyNote: Modelled relative value, not measured sky brightness; terrain shielding and atmosphere are not included. The 5 classes are quintiles of Taiwan's land, not an international dark-sky standard.
legend.mapchallenge.day17.hehuan: Hehuanshan Dark Sky Park (Yuanfeng) falls in the darkest class (0.0044, close to the 0.0047 break).
legend.mapchallenge.day17.groundNote: Transparent = below the satellite's detection threshold (not the same as no light at all); 2025 annual average.
legend.mapchallenge.day17.protected: Protected areas (48, ranked by mean estimated sky glow; click for details)
legend.mapchallenge.day17.source: Night lights: NASA Black Marble VNP46A4 (2025 composite); protected areas: national park headquarters, MOA Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency (OGDL 1.0)
legend.mapchallenge.day17.roadsTitle: Roads Where Satellites See No Light
legend.mapchallenge.day17.low: Low radiance (0–3 nW, hidden by default)
legend.mapchallenge.day17.lowNote: "Low" only means the satellite sees weak light: in the New Taipei calibration, 84% of low-radiance samples still had a city streetlight within 230 m, so only "0" is drawn by default (just 2 of 46 such samples had a light nearby). Turn on low via the display setting.
legend.mapchallenge.day17.roadsStats: 2025: 1,520 km (3.34%) of provincial, county and township-class roads were not detected by satellite, in 353 continuous runs of ≥ 1 km; the longest is Provincial Highway 8 (Central Cross-Island Highway), 49.9 km.
legend.mapchallenge.day17.pixelNote: One satellite pixel is about 460 m, too coarse to see a single streetlight, so this does not mean there are no streetlights.
legend.mapchallenge.day17.roadsSource: Night lights: NASA Black Marble VNP46A4 (2025 composite); roads: OpenStreetMap (ODbL); calibration: New Taipei streetlights (data.gov.tw 123962)
legend.mapchallenge.day17.nightFallNote: Simulated by sun elevation; brightness is the 2025 annual average, not an hourly observation.
legend.mapchallenge.day17.nightFallRule: Transparent while the sun is above the horizon, fully lit at 8° below; each place lights up by its own longitude and latitude, east first.
legend.mapchallenge.day17.nightFallTip: Turn on Fishing Lights in the ships layer to see fishing-boat lights at sea.
legend.mapchallenge.day17.nightFallSourc: NASA Black Marble VNP46A4 (2025 composite); sun elevation from an astronomical formula
legend.mapchallenge.day17.ledSub: LED share of electricity = LED kWh ÷ total streetlight kWh (flat-rate + metered + LED)
legend.mapchallenge.day17.ledNote: Counts Taipower streetlight contracts; one contract can cover many lamps. LEDs use less power, so the electricity share understates the lamp share. Private streetlights are excluded.
legend.mapchallenge.day17.ledSource: Taiwan Power Company, streetlight electricity use by county (data.gov.tw 152419, Open Government Data License v1.0)
legend.mapchallenge.day19.complaintsCase: {n} odor complaints; {drawn} drawn on the grid (areas with fewer than 3 distinct locations are not drawn)
legend.mapchallenge.day19.colorIsTop: Colour = most frequent category in the cell
legend.mapchallenge.day19.densTitleCat: Shade = complaints of this category per km²
legend.mapchallenge.day19.gridNote: Cells vary in size: a cell with fewer than 3 distinct reported locations is merged into a larger one (about 0.1 → 0.7 → 5 km²), so large cells mean sparse complaints.
legend.mapchallenge.day19.repeatNote: The same place can be reported repeatedly; more complaints does not mean the worst smell.
legend.mapchallenge.day19.julyNote: July 2026 was not published (not covered); not added to 2025.
legend.mapchallenge.day19.complaintsSour: Source: Ministry of Environment pollution complaint map (data.gov.tw 6390) · Open Government Data License v1.0
legend.mapchallenge.day19.potentialMetho: 500 m cells; livestock by TEDS 13.0 ammonia emissions, facilities by weight, fading with distance (1.2 km decay, 6 km cutoff); wind versions push odor downwind.
legend.mapchallenge.day19.assumedWeight: Facility weights are assumed values (in brackets)
legend.mapchallenge.day19.dumping: Registered waste dumping site (not in potential)
legend.mapchallenge.day19.validation: Check: the top 10% cells hold 31% of livestock & compost complaints but only 1.1% of cooking-fume complaints.
legend.mapchallenge.day19.islands: Potential is a relative ranking, not measured concentration; outlying islands not covered.
legend.mapchallenge.day19.potentialSourc: Sources: TEDS 13.0, ERA5 (Copernicus/ECMWF via Open-Meteo), landfills, incinerators, public sewage plants, slaughterhouses, feed mills, registered waste dumping sites (WR_P_244) · Open Government Data License v1.0
legend.mapchallenge.day19.penaltiesSub: {f} facilities, {n} penalties (since 2017); colour = highest exceedance ratio
legend.mapchallenge.day19.penaltiesNote: Only penalties whose facts mention odor pollutants; the facts field exists from 2017 and is about 60% blank, so 848 is a lower bound. Individually run livestock farms are not named.
legend.mapchallenge.day19.penaltiesSourc: Source: Ministry of Environment enforcement penalties · Open Government Data License v1.0
legend.mapchallenge.day21.title: When Roads Were Drawn into OSM
legend.mapchallenge.day21.colorNote: Colour = the year this road segment was first drawn in OpenStreetMap; one cell per year, years with more new roads span more of the ramp.
legend.mapchallenge.day21.yearNote: The year is when the road was drawn into OSM, not when it opened; 2007 means 2007 or earlier; data to 2026-07-27.
legend.mapchallenge.day21.limits: Only roads that still exist on 2026-07-27 ({km} km); deleted roads are not shown. Early years (2007–2011) are slightly overcounted because single lines were later split into two carriageways; a road redrawn at a new position counts as newly drawn. Taipei, New Taipei and Keelung only.
legend.mapchallenge.day21.source: Source: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); history via the ohsome API (HeiGIT)
legend.mapchallenge.day23.termRow: Registered eateries whose name contains “{term}”: {n} ({m} with coordinates, shown on the map)
legend.mapchallenge.day23.termNote.yiMia: “意麵” excludes names that also contain “鍋燒”.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.termNote.banTi: The two spellings “粄條” and “板條” are counted together.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.sizeTitle: Circle size = shops in the hexagon (area proportional to count)
legend.mapchallenge.day23.gridNote: Circles sit at hexagon centres, not at shop locations. Zoomed out, each cell is about 36 km²; from zoom 9 the grid switches to cells of about 5.2 km². Cells with only 1–2 shops are drawn too.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.scope: Only registered eateries whose name contains the word are counted; street vendors and shops whose name does not mention the dish are not included; this does not indicate taste preference.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.base: Base: {n} businesses in the Ministry of Finance tax registry ({date}) that are operating and whose main industry is food service. Shop names and addresses are not shown.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.source: Source: Fiscal Information Agency, Ministry of Finance, national business (tax) registration data · Open Government Data License v1.0
legend.mapchallenge.day23.variantsNote: Each colour is one spelling; when a cell has several spellings, the circles stack on the same cell centre. A name containing two spellings is counted once for each.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.group.rice: 魯肉飯／滷肉飯／肉燥飯 (braised or minced pork over rice)
legend.mapchallenge.day23.group.banTiao: 粄條／板條 (Hakka flat rice noodles)
legend.mapchallenge.day23.group.kongRou: 爌肉／焢肉／控肉 (braised pork belly)
legend.mapchallenge.day23.termNote.salte: The two spellings “塩水雞” and “鹽水雞” are counted together.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.placeRow: Sign “{sign}”: {n} registered eateries nationwide, of which {out} are registered outside {home} ({m} shown on the map). Only those outside shops are drawn.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.originRow: Hollow circle: location of the place named in the shop name
legend.mapchallenge.day23.dotRow: Glowing dots: shops registered outside {home} that carry this sign (aggregated to hexagons)
legend.mapchallenge.day23.arcRow: Arcs: link the place name to each cell with such shops; thicker means more shops in that cell
legend.mapchallenge.day23.arcNote: The arcs only link the place named in the shop name to the cell where the shop is; they do not represent movement of people or goods.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.placesScope: Only registered eateries whose name contains both the place name and the dish, and that are registered outside the home county, are counted; street vendors are not included; a place name in a shop name does not mean the owner or ingredients come from there.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.foreignTitle: Foreign Cuisine Words in Shop Names
legend.mapchallenge.day23.foreignRow: “{group}” group: {n} registered eateries whose name contains any of the words below ({m} with coordinates, shown on the map)
legend.mapchallenge.day23.foreignWords: Words matched: {words}. A name containing any one of them counts; each shop is counted once.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.foreignDominan: About {pct}% of this group ({hits} of {n}) are shops whose name contains “{word}”.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.foreignSizeNot: Groups with many shops are drawn smaller overall (each group has its own circle scale), so circle sizes cannot be compared between groups.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.foreignScope: Only registered eateries whose name contains these words are counted; street vendors and shops whose name does not say so are not included; the word lists were chosen by hand and will both miss and wrongly include some shops; this does not indicate the owner’s nationality or taste preference.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.sign.chishang: 池上 (Chishang) + 飯包／便當 (boxed meal)
legend.mapchallenge.day23.sign.meinong: 美濃 (Meinong) + 粄條 (flat rice noodles)
legend.mapchallenge.day23.signRule.chish: Match: the name contains “池上” and either “飯包” or “便當”.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.signRule.chiay: Match: the name contains “嘉義” and “雞肉飯”. Both Chiayi City and Chiayi County count as home.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.signRule.taina: Match: the name contains “臺南” or “台南”, and “虱目魚”.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.signRule.gangs: Match: the name contains “岡山” and “羊肉”.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.signRule.chang: Match: the name contains “彰化” and “肉圓”.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.signRule.dongs: Match: the name contains “東石” or “布袋”, and “蚵”. Both Chiayi City and Chiayi County count as home.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.signRule.beiga: Match: the name contains “北港”; any dish.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.signRule.meino: Match: the name contains “美濃” and either “粄條” or “板條”.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.title.gb: Tastes in UK food business names
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.term.gb.f: fish and chip shop, Yorkshire usage
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.termRow: Shops whose name contains “{term}”: {n} (of which {m} have coordinates and are drawn)
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.sizeNote: Words with many shops are drawn smaller overall (each word, and the large and small cells, have their own size ratio), so circle sizes cannot be compared between words, countries or zoom levels.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.gridNote: Dots sit at hexagon centres, not at shop locations. Cells with only 1–2 shops are drawn too.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.scope: Only shops whose name contains the word are counted; this does not indicate taste preference.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.where.kr: Data covers South Korea only; move the map to South Korea to see the dots.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.where.gb: Data covers the United Kingdom only; move the map to the UK to see the dots.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.where.jp: Data covers Japan only; move the map to Japan to see the dots.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.limits.kr: The base includes cafés and bars. From 2026 Gwangju and Jeonnam are merged, so there are 16 province-level regions.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.limits.gb: About 11% of shops have no coordinates in the API and are not on the map. The base includes pubs.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.limits.jp: OSM is mapped by volunteers and is not a national register; cities and tourist areas are covered more completely, so the numbers should not be set side by side with other countries.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.base.kr: Base: {n} shops in the major category “음식” (food service, including cafés, bars and staff canteens); reference date {date} (updated quarterly). Shop names and addresses are not shown.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.base.gb: Base: {n} businesses of type Restaurant/Cafe/Canteen, Takeaway/sandwich shop or Pub/bar/nightclub, of which {xy} have coordinates; API retrieved {date}. Shop names and addresses are not shown.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.base.jp: Base: {n} OSM features with amenity = restaurant / fast_food / cafe / food_court / pub / bar inside the 47 prefectures (95% have a name); Overpass retrieved {date}. Shop names and addresses are not shown.
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.source.kr: Data: 소상공인시장진흥공단 (Small Enterprise and Market Service), “상가(상권)정보” (2026-09-30), public data portal data.go.kr · Licence: “이용허락범위 제한 없음” (scope of permitted use: no restriction)
legend.mapchallenge.day23.intl.source.gb: Contains Food Standards Agency data (Food Hygiene Rating Scheme), licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. © Crown copyright
